title: Shift-dragging a marquee adds what it sweeps to the selection
goal: Sweeping a marquee always starts the selection over, and a shift-click on empty space throws the whole selection away, so one slightly-off click undoes careful picking. Holding shift while you sweep should add what the band takes in to what is already picked, and a shift-click that lands on nothing should leave the selection alone.
notes: Today shift over an empty press means constrain-the-band-to-a-square (CanvasView.mouseUp reads .shift for that), so the square constraint needs a new home or has to go. mouseDown else-branch calls onClickedNothing()/onSelectLayer(nil) before starting the MarqueeDrag, and mouseUp commits a click as commitSelection(nil, capture: true) which is what wipes the selection. EditorState.setSelection(_:captureLayers:) would need an additive mode that unions with multiSelectedLayerIDs. Noticed while building canvas shift-click (2026-09-03).
acceptance: Shift-dragging a band on the canvas adds every layer it fully contains to the existing selection
A shift-click that lands on empty canvas leaves the selection exactly as it was
A plain sweep still replaces the selection the way it does today
The outlines after a shift-sweep show every picked layer, swept or clicked
